title: SD: system suite — test/system/harbour-halt.test.js fails on clean main (not host-related, cause unknown)
description:
## Problem

`test/system/harbour-halt.test.js` fails under `npm run test:system`: the Harbour-side halt system test (LIN-3044). The assertion that a follow-up stays queued and unclaimed under a Harbour halt fails (assertion `the follow-up is still queued, unclaimed`, `test/system/harbour-halt.test.js:176`).

## Why it matters

Same stop control as `halt-mechanism`, exercised through Harbour's per-token halt. The two may share a cause; check that first, and if so merge the tickets (link as duplicate) rather than fix twice. The system suite is also the only place these behaviours are exercised end to end, and nothing automated watches it.

## Reproduces on

Repo: **JKershaw/simple-dispatcher**. `npm run test:system` (not in CI; `ci.yml` runs only `npm test`), with `HARBOUR_DIR` pointing at a LinearViewer checkout. Measured by LIN-4181 (merged as PR #309, `11a1279`) on the runner host:

* identical on clean `main` (`0992f39`) and on the LIN-4181 head, run from a workspace clone, a checkout in `/private/tmp`, and a checkout with `TMPDIR` inside `state/`;
* identical against Harbour `9e397e6b`, `10b2c82f` and `0dc1620e`;
* each also fails when its file is run on its own.
  So it is **not** host or location noise, **not** Harbour-version skew and **not** a LIN-4181 regression. The cause is **not known**: LIN-4181 triaged it only far enough to rule those out.

## Acceptance

* The cause is found and stated on this ticket: a real Simple Dispatcher defect, a real Harbour defect (then a Harbour ticket exists), or drift between the test and Harbour.
* `test/system/harbour-halt.test.js` passes against the Harbour checkout it is run with, **or** is skipped with a stated, checked reason. It is not loosened to pass: the assertion on line 176 keeps guarding what it guards.
* `npm run test:system` no longer lists `harbour-halt` among its failures, run from a workspace clone, with the other three named failures treated separately.

## Anchors

* `test/system/harbour-halt.test.js:176`
* `test/system/harness/harbour.js` (how Harbour is started), `test/system/README.md`
* Related: LIN-2471 (an earlier, different red case in the same suite), LIN-4181 (found this; the triage is in its review comments and close-out)

## Unvalidated idea

None worth stating: the cause is unknown. A first step is to run this file alone with Harbour's logs kept and look at what the queue/feed holds at the failing assertion.

---

*Priority: priorityLevel 3 (High): same reasoning as* `halt-mechanism` *(guards the halt/stop control); cause unknown. Label: Bug (the workspace catalog has no narrower type label).*

comments.body:
**Cause found: drift between this test and the dispatcher's own LIN-4079 rule. Not a halt defect, not Harbour.** PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/316

- LIN-4079 (`bd6d2cf`, #299) made a follow-up to a CANCELLED session a **reject** verdict (`session-stopped`, terminal `[failed]`), never a resume.
- A stop cancels the parent, so the parent's follow-up is no longer a resume. `halt-stop-followup-hold` only holds resume verdicts, so the follow-up is claimed and refused instead of staying queued. Seen directly: in cycle 2 the item's history shows `status: taken` with no launch.
- LIN-4079 rewrote the unit twins of this case in `test/lin-3043-stop-sweep.test.js` ("all-held #3", "decision 9") but not the system-suite copies, which are not in CI.

**Witness:** at `bd6d2cf^`, `harbour-halt` and `halt-mechanism` pass 9/9. At `bd6d2cf`, exactly the two named tests fail.

**Fix (tests only):** cycle 2 now asserts: no launch, the parent stays CANCELLED, and the follow-up leaves the queue with `[failed] Cannot follow up: session <id> was cancelled`. This keeps guarding what line 176 guarded (a follow-up never undoes the stop's cancel) and adds the end-to-end refusal. With LIN-4079's rule undone in `followup.js`, the rewritten tests fail.

After the fix, `npm run test:system` is 117/119. The two remaining reds (Observation feed, Tap 1 OpenRouter) are unrelated. LIN-4185 had the same cause, so it is linked as a duplicate and fixed in the same PR.

Closing: the red `harbour-halt` baseline was fixed by PR #316 (merged 2026-11-04T07:41:45Z, tests only), and PR #313 (LIN-4196), which it blocked, has now merged as `502901c`. The real gate's baseline ran 25/25 green with it.
